messages:
maya: @acme-infra we got your ticket — can you paste the exact request + response? you mentioned it started after yesterday's model swap.
acme-infra: Repro steps:
1) POST /v1/generate with {"model":"redwood-4.1.3", "json_mode": true, "prompt": "..." }
2) Receive 400 with body:
```
ERROR: invalid JSON
{"items": [{"id":"123", "details": null,
 "notes":"Line1
Line2"}]}
```
We see a raw newline in the notes field (unescaped), parser throws. Also token usage shot from ~200 to ~1200 on our bill.
maya: thanks. did you try pinning the previous model to confirm? does that stop the failure?
acme-infra: pinned to 4.1.2 -> works fine. so the behaviour started exactly when traffic moved to 4.1.3.
jonathan: tagging eng-runtime. any recent changes to postproc/escape handling? could be sampling now emitting raw newlines in generation for that field.
aisha: FYI I'm also seeing elevated p95 latency for the 4.1.3 pool in us-west-2 during the rollout window, some requests falling back to a slower replica. logs show request_id=abc-123 timed out after 15s.
jonathan: can you paste the raw response bytes/headers for request_id=abc-123? need content-type & content-length.
maya: attached the raw response in the ticket. headers show Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8, Content-Length: 842, but body includes unescaped multiline value.
jonathan: quick hypothesis: a postprocessing step that used to escape control chars was bypassed for long-ish tokens after a change in the kernel selection logic. the model now emits a literal newline token inside the "notes" generation. our JSON serializer relied on escaping at a later stage which got short-circuited.
support-bot: action created INC-4123 assigned_to: eng-runtime priority: high impact: customer-visible JSON parse errors
jonathan: proposed short-term mitigation: server-side param to normalize multiline strings. we'll add a temporary backfill that replaces raw newlines with \n when json_mode=true. canary deploy planned in ~1 hour. also advise customer to pin to 4.1.2 for now.
maya: informed customer of the pin workaround and ETA. they asked about billing impact — said quota alerts triggered due to token spike.
acme-infra: pin fixed parsing but billing alert already fired. can you confirm there's no weird double-encoding causing extra tokens?
jonathan: investigating token accounting; initial look suggests the model inserted long whitespace sequences and extra unescaped characters which expanded tokenization. also one of our escape passes may have been removed, causing sequences to be emitted literally instead of as escaped sequences, increasing token count.
aisha: routing note: about 30% of requests during the incident were served by a fallback region, which bumped latency and could exacerbate retries. we'll reconcile traces.
jonathan: next steps: 1) reproduce locally with the exact request+seed, 2) add unit test for json_mode to catch raw newline emission, 3) patch postproc to escape control chars consistently, 4) canary fix + rollback plan, 5) mitigation to rewrite newlines to \n for active customers.
maya: I'll keep customer updated and will provide the incident ticket link. if they want immediate relief we can issue a temporary billing credit or quota override.
acme-infra: thanks — pin + canary plan is fine. please ping when canary is live. :thumbsup:
jonathan: will post canary link and monitor token usage + parse error rate.
__notes: thread about structured output regression after model upgrade; contains repro, raw response snippet, mitigation, and action items
